blocks.text: The curtain rises slowly. The scene is the same as at the close of the second day, on the Valkyries’ rock; night. In the background, from below, firelight shines. The three Norns, tall women in long, dark, veil-like drapery. The first (eldest) lies in the foreground, to the right, under the spreading pine-tree; the second (younger) is stretched on a shelving rock in front of the cave; the third (youngest) sits in the centre at the back on a rock near the peak. Motionless, gloomy silence.

lines: Glows in flame around the rock.
Why spin we not, singing the while?
Where for our spinning and singing

blocks.text: While she loosens a golden rope from herself and ties one end of it to a branch of the pine-tree.

lines: I sing and wind the rope
Badly or well, as may be.
The boughs of a sacred wood.
Came to drink at the well;
He paid with the loss of an eye.
And shaped the shaft of a spear.
As time rolled on the wood
Wasted and died of the wound;
Here on the pine-tree my rope.

blocks.text: Winds the rope thrown to her round a projecting rock at the entrance of the cave.

lines: Which wielding, he swayed the world.
In fight then splintered the spear,
With its treaties cleaving in twain.
Both the stem and boughs sere and barren.
Sealed was the fountain that flowed.
Of the rock I wind the rope:

blocks.text: Catching the rope and throwing the end behind her.

lines: With the Gods and the holy
Shall the fair hall be consumed.
And then shall the high Gods’ downfall
Spin and sing, O my sister.

blocks.text: She throws the rope to the second Norn and the second throws it to the first, who loosens the rope from the bough and ties it on to another.

lines: Dost thou know how he fared?

blocks.text: Winding the rope which has been thrown to her round the rock again.

lines: The solemn runes on the shaft.
Canst thou tell us the end?
The blazing one deep in the breast;
Hewn logs heaped ready for burning.

blocks.text: She throws the rope back; the second Norn winds it up and throws it again to the first.

lines: The strands are twisted and loose.

blocks.text: With laborious haste winds the rope round the jagged rock at the mouth of the cave.
Hastily catching the rope which is thrown to her.

lines: Its end can reach to the north!

blocks.text: She pulls hard at the rope, which breaks.
They take the pieces of broken rope and bind their bodies together with them.
They vanish. The dawn grows brighter; the firelight from the valley gradually fades. Sunrise; then broad daylight.
Siegfried and Brünnhilde enter from the cave. He is fully armed; she leads her horse by the bridle.

lines: The things the Gods taught me
Thy gifts than I can guard!
O chide not if thy teaching
To that lore I hold fast;
And one lesson I have learned—
If thou wouldst truly love me,
And of thy deeds of daring!
That fearless thou didst fare through
When around the rock it burned—
Think too of the shield-hidden maid
Thou didst find there lapped in slumber.
And whose helmet hard thou didst break—
Will deeply burn then for aye!
Must I leave thee, O love,
In thy holy fortress of fire,

blocks.text: He has taken Alberich’s ring from his finger, and holds it out to Brünnhilde.

lines: This ring of mine I give thee;
Let it pay for thy runes.
By my hand was the dragon grim,
Who long had guarded it, slain;
Keep thou the gold and its might
As token true of my love!

blocks.text: Putting on the ring in rapturous delight.

lines: I covet it more than all else!
For the ring take Grane, my horse.
But if thou lead the way,
Then every deed that I dare
Will be achieved through thy virtue
All my battles thou wilt choose,
And my victories will be thine.
O were but Brünnhilde thy soul too!
Through her my courage burns high.
Then wert thou Siegfried and Brünnhild’.
Where I am, there thy abode is.
Then a waste is my hall of rock?

blocks.text: Siegfried leads the horse quickly to the edge of the sloping rock, Brünnhilde following him. Siegfried disappears with the horse down behind the projecting rock, so that he is no longer visible to the audience. Brünnhilde is thus suddenly left standing alone on the edge of the slope, and gazes down into the valley after Siegfried. Her gestures show that Siegfried has vanished from her sight. Siegfried’s horn is heard from below. Brünnhilde listens, and steps further out on the slope. She catches sight of Siegfried in the valley again, and waves to him joyfully. Her happy smiles seem to reflect the air of the merrily departing hero.
